title: Area of trapeziums, rhombuses and kites

draft.title: Area of trapeziums, rhombuses and kites
card: A = ½ × (a + b) × h. Here a and b are the two parallel sides, and h is the height, measured at right angles to them.
A = ½ × d₁ × d₂. Here d₁ and d₂ are the two diagonals, the lines joining opposite corners.
Example: a trapezium has parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm and a height of 4 cm. A = ½ × (6 + 10) × 4 = ½ × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².
Example: a kite has diagonals 8 cm and 5 cm. A = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm².
draft.remember: Trapezium: half the sum of the parallel sides times height. Rhombus and kite: half the product of the diagonals.

a.q: A rhombus has diagonals of 12 cm and 7 cm. What is its area?
a.why: A = ½ × 12 × 7 = 42 cm². Using 12 × 7 = 84 cm² forgets to halve the product.
a.clue: Multiply the diagonals, then take half.

b.q: Mia's garden bed is a trapezium. Its parallel sides are 9 m and 5 m, and the slanted side is 4 m. The height is 3 m. What is its area?
b.why: A = ½ × (9 + 5) × 3 = ½ × 14 × 3 = 21 m². The slanted side is not the height, so using 4 m gives 28 m², which is wrong.
b.clue: The height meets the parallel sides at right angles.
